title: A Sinclair Henderson Trust

title: Adint Charitable Trust

title: AF3: Supporting Partners programme
brief_what_they_fund: Projects that strengthen support for partners of serving military personnel (including reservists) by improving access to employment support, building skills and confidence, addressing barriers to career change, and enhancing mental health and wellbeing. Projects can be regional, national, or serve armed forces communities based overseas.

title: AI For All
brief_what_they_fund: UK charities working to create greater access, opportunity, and representation in technology and AI. Support areas include digital inclusion, education and skills, social mobility, disability inclusion, gender equity, racial equity, community development, and future workforce readiness.

title: Albert Gubay Charitable Foundation Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Charitable projects and programmes run by registered charities across England, Wales, the Isle of Man, and the Republic of Ireland. The foundation supports a wide range of causes to help charities develop and maintain their inspiring work.

title: Aldi Scottish Sport Fund — North-East, Highlands and Islands
brief_what_they_fund: Grants to help registered community sports organisations with essentials like equipment, kits, training costs and more, encouraging participation for all ages and abilities.

title: An Official Oral History of Women Veterans in the UK
brief_what_they_fund: An official oral history project documenting the lived experiences of women veterans in the UK Armed Forces, including interview recordings, transcripts, digital resources, exhibitions and educational materials.

title: Ancaster Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Grants to charitable organisations for general charitable purposes, advancement of health or saving of lives, disability, overseas aid/famine relief, and arts/culture/heritage/science.

title: Army Benevolent Fund Charity Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Grants to charities and organisations that provide services and support to the Army family: serving soldiers, former soldiers, and their immediate families (including the bereaved). The fund supports core operating costs and contributions to organisations' general salary costs as part of operating costs.

title: Arts Council of Wales — Have a Go
brief_what_they_fund: One-off hands-on arts activities or workshops for young people aged 3–16 in the five disciplines of the Expressive Arts Area of Learning and Experience: art, dance, drama, film and digital media, and music. title: Arts Council of Wales — International Opportunities Fund
brief_what_they_fund: In-person arts activity taking place outside Wales and the UK that involves international collaboration, partnership development, participation in international networks and events, presentation of work, or international residencies. Activity must involve at least one international partner and demonstrate clear artistic benefit.

title: Austin and Hope Pilkington Trust Unpaid Carers Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Registered UK charities working with communities on specific annual priorities. For 2026 Rounds 3 and 4, this grant funds projects providing therapeutic support to unpaid adult carers, including healthy eating and outdoor activities.

title: Barbara Ward Children's Foundation
brief_what_they_fund: Charitable activities and projects that help severely disadvantaged children. They support smaller non-religious charities focused on direct service delivery to vulnerable young people.

title: Baring Foundation — Strengthening Civil Society Programme
brief_what_they_fund: Civil society organisations using legal tools and human rights-based approaches to hold corporations accountable for harms caused to migrant communities. This includes legal research, bringing legal challenges against companies acting unlawfully, supporting non-legal organisations to use regulators, and monitoring implementation of legal wins. Work must seek to address discrimination and deliver broader social change affecting communities or large numbers of people, not individual service delivery.

title: BE:IMPACT Prize 2026
brief_what_they_fund: UK charity campaigns that are already creating meaningful, measurable impact. The prize supports charities ready to reach more people with their work and increase visibility of their campaigns.

title: Beinneun Community Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Community projects and activities that benefit residents of Glengarry, Fort Augustus and Glenmoriston in Highland. The fund supports both single-year projects and multi-year strategic initiatives, including governance and organisational development, environmental sustainability projects, and climate action at local level.

title: Bernard Sunley Foundation — Social Welfare Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Grants to assist vulnerable groups including people experiencing homelessness, addiction, domestic and sexual abuse survivors, ex-offenders, elderly people, armed forces veterans, those in poverty, animal welfare, almshouses, and social enterprises.

title: Bolton Housing Partnership — Community Investment Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Projects that make a difference to Bolton Housing Partnership tenants and their communities: new equipment or materials, running a community event, launching a new group, or promoting existing ones. Your project must help people in at least one of six ways: health and wellbeing, children and young people, cost of living support, training and employment skills, connecting communities, or the environment. The funder is explicit that it is "better to meet one theme very well rather than all of them loosely". Up to 50% of an award may go towards core running costs, including energy, fuel, rent, food, services, volunteer expenses and paying staff a living wage.

title: C B & H H Taylor 1984 Trust — Grants
funder: C B & H H Taylor 1984 Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Grants supporting Religious Society of Friends (Quaker) work; charities serving the West Midlands (Birmingham, Coventry, Wolverhampton, Dudley, Sandwell, Solihull, Walsall); charities working in specified African countries and the Indian subcontinent; and humanitarian emergency aid. Within these areas: social welfare (children, young people, older people, disabilities, homelessness, women-led initiatives, counselling, hospice services); education (adult literacy, employment training, youth work, mental health education); penal affairs (work with offenders and ex-offenders, families of offenders, youth projects); and social, ecological and agriculture initiatives.

title: Castle Studies Trust Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Projects that enhance understanding and knowledge of castles, including architectural and geophysical surveys, scientific tests such as radio-carbon dating, and reconstruction drawings to enhance public understanding.

title: Chichester District Council — Community Grants Programme
Childs Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Christian organisations that actively share the Christian gospel message. The Trust strategically funds work aligned with their vision of helping every person hear and respond to the gospel.

title: City Bridge Foundation — Climate & Environmental Justice (Round One)
brief_what_they_fund: Community-led organisations delivering climate and environmental justice work in London through place-based resilience, community organising and influence, or storytelling and narrative change. Work must address immediate climate and environmental harms while contributing to longer-term systems change.

title: City Bridge Foundation Communities Building Economic Change
brief_what_they_fund: Community-led and grassroots organisations tackling the root causes of economic injustice in London. They fund work that addresses poverty, income inequality, job insecurity, debt, and the systemic policies and power dynamics that perpetuate economic disadvantage.

title: Comic Relief Community Fund England
brief_what_they_fund: Community-led projects that drive change in local communities. The 2026/27 programme prioritises tackling homelessness, supporting those experiencing cost of living concerns, early childhood development initiatives, and projects preventing violence against women and girls, or supporting refugees and asylum seekers.

title: Cornwall Community Foundation — Community Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Cornwall CF runs several concurrently-open grant funds: general/unrestricted community projects (Carew Pole), financial hardship, debt and fuel poverty (Resilience Fund), and children & young people, community facilities and health (Cornish Lithium Community Fund), plus individual-focused crisis and talent funds. Across its portfolio it backs charities and community groups improving life for residents of Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly.

title: Cuthbert Horn Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Projects run by voluntary and community organisations. The Trust does not specify particular cause areas or project types beyond general charitable work.

title: DCMS 'Connections Through Gaming' Pilot Fund (Boys 11-16)
funder: Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport
brief_what_they_fund: Three-year pilot programme combining gaming-based activities with structured wellbeing and confidence-building support to engage boys aged 11–16 experiencing loneliness, isolation or low wellbeing. Funding covers in-person delivery in youth-focused settings plus secure online provision, delivered by experienced youth engagement organisations.

title: Dixie Rose Findlay Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: General charitable purposes. The trust supports a diverse range of registered charities across the UK, including organisations working in audio accessibility, children's services, disability support, hospice care, emergency services, and community facilities.

title: Education Foundation For John Vaughan
brief_what_they_fund: Non-statutory education and lifelong learning, including early years provision. Also supports spiritual wellbeing and improving the lives of people with limited resources.

title: Eleanor Rathbone Charitable Trust — General Grants
brief_what_they_fund: The source does not explicitly state funding priorities or themes. Check the 'Guidelines for Applicants' and 'Exclusions' sections on their website for details of what the trust supports.

title: Emerton-Christie Charity
brief_what_they_fund: Grants to UK-registered charities across a range of causes including education and training, health, disability support, arts, culture, heritage, science, and environment/conservation.

title: Eranda Rothschild Foundation
brief_what_they_fund: The Foundation supports registered charities working in three fields: medical research (original research, continuation of existing research, and welfare); education (support for young professionals in medicine, science and business, disadvantaged young people, and apprenticeships); and the arts (education and outreach work of arts charities).

title: Ernest Kleinwort Charitable Trust Medium Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Charities supporting beneficiaries in Sussex; wildlife and environmental conservation projects (UK or international); reproductive health and family planning projects in Africa or Asia with clear environmental impact.

title: Esmée Fairbairn Foundation — A Fairer Future
brief_what_they_fund: Organisations working towards social change across four priority areas: arts and creativity making change; children and young people's rights; racial justice; and gender justice, migrant justice, and related systemic injustice. Support focuses on tackling systemic injustice and building capacity of underrepresented communities.

title: Farmer Welfare Grant
funder: Department for Environment, Food and Rural Affairs
brief_what_they_fund: Projects that support the mental health and wellbeing of agricultural workers, farmers, and farming families. title: Fine & Country Foundation — Homelessness Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Charities working on prevention of homelessness, care of the homeless, or constructive projects to get homeless people off the streets permanently. Eligible organisations include homeless charities, poverty prevention schemes, and housing associations.

title: Fitton Trust
brief_what_they_fund: General charitable purposes. The trust supports legally charitable institutions across a broad spectrum of causes at the trustees' discretion.

title: Forever Manchester — Community Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Community activity and projects across Greater Manchester. Forever Manchester manages and administers a range of funds supporting community building, asset-based community development, and training initiatives.

title: Funding for STEM activities in the North East
funder: Community Foundation Tyne & Wear and Northumberland
brief_what_they_fund: STEM (science, technology, engineering, and mathematics) activities and training, including vocational-based trades. The fund also supports celebrating STEM heritage. Applications focus on education and training projects, particularly around engineering.

title: Gatsby Charitable Foundation
brief_what_they_fund: Projects and interventions across six focus areas: Education, Neuroscience, Plant Science, Africa, Public Policy, and Arts. Gatsby typically commissions research and designs interventions in partnership with sector and industry experts.

title: Grassroots Grants
brief_what_they_fund: A wide range of local projects and activities. The Grassroots Grants fund is designed to be flexible and accessible, supporting grassroots organisations that understand what their communities need.

title: Green Community Grants Programme

brief_what_they_fund: Projects that contribute to nature recovery and respond to the climate emergency, or that improve nature-rich spaces and access to them. Funding can also support wider sustainable activities including recycling, litter picking, beach cleans, and sustainable transport.

A Small Grants Programme also provides smaller grants for community-led activities and local projects.

title: Heart Research UK — Healthy Hearts Grants (Northern Ireland)
brief_what_they_fund: Community projects that promote heart health and reduce the risk of heart disease in adults (18+). Projects may include other health and wellbeing aspects but must centre on these four key risk factors.

title: Henry Smith Foundation Domestic Abuse Counselling Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Long-term counselling services for survivors of domestic abuse. The fund specifically targets specialist domestic abuse organisations providing counselling support.

title: Herefordshire Community Foundation — Community Grants (Community Chest)
brief_what_they_fund: Community and voluntary groups, charities and individuals working on projects that strengthen communities in Herefordshire.

title: Hollick Family Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Charitable projects and activities in their geographic areas of focus.

title: Ian Askew Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Grants to organisations working with children and young people, older people, disability and health care, and welfare.

title: Ilford Community Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Activities and services that address cost of living, food insecurity, community safety and belonging, and loneliness in Ilford. Priority is given to proposals addressing the root causes of these issues.

title: Inman Charity
brief_what_they_fund: Registered charities and CICs working in medical research, care of the elderly, older people and general welfare, hospices, support for the deaf and blind, care of the physically and mentally disabled, and support for the armed forces.

title: James Ahern Foundation
brief_what_they_fund: Small grants to young people to help them pursue their passion in life. They support individuals facing disadvantage who are working towards personal goals.

title: Kusuma Trust UK — Education, Communities & Environment

title: Lambert Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Projects benefiting those in need, with particular interest in medicine, social care, education, disabled persons, homes for the elderly, and charities benefiting people of the Jewish faith.

title: Lambeth Community Connections Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Community-led projects that make their communities better, fairer, and safer. The fund supports local groups with big ideas to strengthen their neighbourhoods.

title: Legal Education Foundation — Strengthening Justice Fund

title: Lewes Fund (via SCF Main Grants)
brief_what_they_fund: Grassroots and community organisations delivering vital work across four priority areas: tackling poverty, improving health, reaching potential (skills, education, training), and acting on climate. Funding supports both core operational costs and project expenses for up to one year.

title: Lush Charity Pot — Grants

Grants specifically support 'non-violent direct action' groups undertaking work that aims to create long-term change and is often unpopular or overlooked by other funders.

title: Magdalen Hospital Trust — Vulnerable Children & Young Adults Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Projects supporting vulnerable children and young adults (male and female), especially those at risk of sexual and other forms of exploitation, and young parents in difficult situations. Examples include out-of-school and after-school support, safeguarding education, personal development, mental health support and counselling.

title: Main Grants - Acting on Climate
brief_what_they_fund: Community organisations working on climate action and environmental issues at a local level across Sussex. This is one of four core funding priorities alongside tackling poverty, improving health, and reaching potential.

title: Make a Difference Locally (MADL)

title: Moondance Foundation — General Funding
brief_what_they_fund: Organisations working in children & young people, community development & participation, education & training, environment/conservation, health (relief & support of illness/sickness), older people, women, and prevention & relief of poverty. Based in Wales.

title: Movement for Good — £1,000 Draws
brief_what_they_fund: Registered charities, non-registered charities, churches, and Community Interest Companies across any cause area. Movement for Good distributes Benefact Group's available profits to good causes through nomination-based draws.

title: NFU Mutual Charitable Trust — December 2026 Funding Round
brief_what_they_fund: Projects and initiatives that support rural communities, with particular emphasis on education of young people in rural areas and relief of poverty in rural settings.

title: Oake Sunshine Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Activities, services, and facilities that benefit residents of the parish of Oake, including the hamlets of Heathfield, Hillcommon, Hillfarrance and Oake. The fund was established through the New Rendy Solar Farm development and has deliberately broad scope.

title: Open Society Foundations — Europe & UK Programmes
brief_what_they_fund: Democratic governance, human rights, justice, equity, and accountability. Open Society supports organisations and individuals working to build vibrant and inclusive democracies, strengthen media freedom, reduce violence, improve government transparency, and increase political participation.

title: Passionate About Realising Potential in environmental/green careers
funder: Community Foundation Tyne & Wear and Northumberland
brief_what_they_fund: Grants to support individuals pursuing careers in environmental and green jobs such as horticulture, parks and gardens, and sustainable energy. Also funds training courses and activities that benefit groups of people with accreditation in these sectors.

title: Pilkington Charities' Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Charities working to help people in Merseyside affected by poverty, old age or ill health, with the aspiration to achieve sustainable improvements in their quality of life.

title: Salford CVS — Grants Programmes
brief_what_they_fund: Health and wellbeing, arts and culture, employment support, drug and alcohol recovery, cancer screening, food banks and holiday activities, family support services, physical activity, mental health, short breaks for children with SEND, and hate crime awareness and reporting.

title: Sea-Changers Main Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Marine conservation projects in the UK that address root causes of marine threats, prevent negative impacts on coastal and marine environments, or add to knowledge about marine conservation. title: Shoosmiths Foundation
brief_what_they_fund: Charities and organisations working in three key areas: social mobility, net zero, and access to justice. The Foundation supports causes that create lasting community change and sustainable impact.

title: Sigrid Rausing Trust — Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Organisations working on human rights and the rule of law, open societies, and environmental protection. The trust supports charities and civil society organisations addressing these themes globally, with particular focus on Central and Eastern Europe and Eurasia.

title: South Yorkshire's Community Foundation — Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Community projects and organisations across South Yorkshire. The foundation offers multiple grant programmes tailored to different scales and types of need, from small grassroots initiatives to larger community-led projects.

title: Steel Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Charitable activity in Luton, and projects for under-26s across the rest of the United Kingdom.

title: Stobart Sustainability Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Community groups, educational facilities, and small businesses with projects and initiatives of a green, ecological, or sustainability nature that benefit the environment.

title: Stronger Communities Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Community projects, charities, and social enterprises delivering work that unites, supports, and protects local people across Manchester. The fund supports causes aligned with community strengthening themes.

title: Sunrise Medical Community Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Projects that help wheelchair users and disabled people enjoy greater independence, inclusion and opportunity. This includes disability sports clubs, community events, specialist mobility equipment, days out and accessible experiences, personal challenges, and local community projects that improve accessibility and inclusion.

title: Supporting community groups within a 10-mile radius of the Green Rigg Wind Farm
funder: Community Foundation Tyne & Wear and Northumberland
brief_what_they_fund: Priority is given to capital items with a tangible, lasting benefit, including improvements to community buildings. funder: Community Foundation Tyne & Wear and Northumberland

title: Supporting the community in the Parish of Shotley Low Quarter
funder: Community Foundation Tyne & Wear and Northumberland
brief_what_they_fund: General running costs, specific projects or activities, and capital developments or equipment. The fund names capital items such as games, resources and equipment, revenue items such as trips and entrance fees, sessional worker costs, repairs and refurbishment of community buildings, start-up costs for new community groups, out-of-school activities, and community and environmental projects.

title: Sussex Community Foundation — Brighton and Hove Legacy Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Projects supporting the personal and educational development of children and young people up to age 25 in Brighton and Hove. Specific focus areas: improving educational attainment, employability and entrepreneurship, participation in positive activities supporting physical and emotional health, volunteering and community engagement, and support for young people facing barriers to achieving their potential.

title: Sussex Crisis Fund — Sussex Community Foundation

title: Swire Charitable Trust — Core Grant Programme
brief_what_they_fund: Charities and organisations working to improve life chances, restore nature, and restore pride to neglected neighbourhoods. The trust supports a range of charitable activities aligned with these three core programmes.

title: Tesco Community Grants (formerly Bags of Help)
brief_what_they_fund: Community projects that benefit local areas, including purchasing equipment and materials, building improvements, outdoor space development, community events, and seasonal activities. Projects must deliver direct community benefit.

title: The Access Foundation
brief_what_they_fund: Charities that make a valuable and measurable positive impact on people's lives. Recent grants include mental health support, digital inclusion initiatives, and support for people with disabilities.

title: The Arts Society External Charity Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Arts organisations, museums, heritage projects and community initiatives focused on public arts or heritage events and festivals that centre on community participation and cohesion, bringing the arts or heritage into shared public places.

title: The Bothwell Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Grants to registered charities supporting disability, social work, children's causes, and hospices.

title: The Grocers' Charity — Small Grants
brief_what_they_fund: The Grocers' Charity funds work aligned with their strategy across philanthropy, education, fellowship, and heritage. They support a range of charitable activities and projects, though specific thematic priorities are not detailed in this excerpt.

title: The Indigo Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Early stage organisations working on systemic injustices in their focus areas: access to justice, racial justice, prevention of child sexual abuse, visual impairment, better grant-making, and women's rights. The Trust supports through flexible grant-making, commissioning research, and building partnerships.

title: The JJ Charitable Trust — Literacy Programme
brief_what_they_fund: Charities and community groups that directly help children and young people develop literacy skills, with a focus on supporting those with learning difficulties such as dyslexia. Projects must support a minimum of 50% children with learning difficulties or who are disengaged from learning, with a clear emphasis on foundational literacy.

title: The Julia Rausing Trust — Grants
brief_what_they_fund: UK charities working across giving themes including learning and development, employment, and spaces where creativity, culture and beauty can be accessed by all with opportunities for active engagement and participation. The Trust makes strategic grants and place-based giving in addition to theme-based support.

title: The Pebble Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Charitable and not-for-profit organisations in Brighton and Hove, particularly those involved in community projects and those working with disadvantaged people. The trust has provided support through talent grants, sponsorship and donations since 2009.

title: The Tedworth Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Projects in parenting, family welfare and child development, arts and the environment. The Trust also supports a small number of projects outside these areas and occasionally responds to international emergency appeals.

title: The Weavers' Company Charitable Funds
brief_what_they_fund: Projects supporting offenders, ex-offenders, and young people at risk of offending into sustainable work and employment. title: The Wyseliot Rose Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Health promotion, life-saving work, the arts, and relief of those in need due to age, ill-health, disability, or other disadvantage.

title: Ufi VocTech Trust — VocTech Activate
brief_what_they_fund: Early-stage innovative digital vocational learning projects. Ufi funds design, development, prototyping and testing of new technology tools or approaches to vocational skills training for adults aged 16+. Projects can involve new technical development, adaptation of existing technology to new markets, or implementation in new learner communities. The emphasis is on genuinely novel ideas that transform vocational learning, particularly for underserved sectors and locations.

title: UK and Ireland Community Tree Planting Grant
Virgin Media O2 - Apprenticeship Talent Fund
brief_what_they_fund: The cost of training an apprentice, paid as a transfer from Virgin Media O2's apprenticeship levy pot. The focus is on getting more women into STEM roles and supporting people from global majority backgrounds into the industry.

title: Wakeham Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Small-scale community projects that create local change. They support initiatives across a range of causes, with particular interest in projects that demonstrate community support and deliver tangible impact.

title: Westminster City Council — Community Grants
brief_what_they_fund: A diverse range of community projects including arts and culture, climate change initiatives, homelessness support, health and wellbeing activities, youth programmes, and social inclusion projects. The council funds capital infrastructure projects, community events, advice services, and core organisational costs for voluntary and community sector organisations.

title: Weston Windfarm Community Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Projects and activities that benefit local residents in the eligible parishes through economic, environmental, educational, social or cultural benefits. Support is available for any type of activity involving local people delivered by small community organisations.

title: Whirlwind Charitable Trust
brief_what_they_fund: Projects improving the lives of disadvantaged children, enhancing lives of those living with disability, and environmental projects with a maritime focus. They support research and conservation initiatives for the maritime environment, and occasionally support highly deserving cases outside their main remit.

title: Worthing Community Chest — Seed Grants
brief_what_they_fund: New and emerging community projects and groups that improve quality of life for disadvantaged people, promote social cohesion, introduce innovative ideas, improve the community, or enhance existing services. Forward-funded grants designed to support groups just starting out.

title: York Community Fund
brief_what_they_fund: Community organisations and groups addressing local need in York through purposeful community action and activities that create a sense of belonging. Funding supports projects tackling affordability and cost of living, climate action, equalities and human rights, and health and wellbeing.

title: Zochonis Charitable Trust — Grants
brief_what_they_fund: Education (school bursaries, learning institutions, artistic and scientific outreach), children and young people support (employment, mental health, social challenges), health (medical research, hospitals, support services), and social equity (human trafficking prevention, poverty and homelessness alleviation) — primarily benefiting people in Greater Manchester.
